podcast.title: Florence Greenberg's Second Label
podcast.body: Scepter Records was Florence Greenberg's new record label, which she started after Decca Records dropped The Shirelles. She re-signed the group to Scepter after they were released from Decca. "Greenberg had remained their manager and she had started up a new record label, SEPTRA Records and signed them up to that instead of TRA."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 89: "Will You Love Me Tomorrow?" by the Shirelles

podcast.title: Impact of Staffing Change
podcast.body: A change in Scepter's staffing, specifically the hiring of Wally Roker as A&R director and his introduction of Luther Dixon, profoundly changed the label's fortunes and the world of music, leading to The Shirelles' greatest successes. "Their first few singles for SEPTRA did nothing but then a change in SEPTRA's staffing changed everything not just for the Chirrells but for the world of music."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Initially Ignored The Kingsmen
podcast.body: Jerry Denon submitted The Kingsmen's "Louie Louie" to Scepter Records, a larger independent label, but they initially "stuck it in a drawer and forgot about it." "He also sent it out to bigger indie labels like Cepter, who stuck it in a drawer and forgot about it"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Luther Dixon's Production and Writing
podcast.body: A significant portion of the material released on Scepter Records was produced and written by Luther Dixon, indicating his influential role at the label. "produced and written, like much of the material on Scepter, by Luther Dixon."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: National Distribution for The Kingsmen (Wand subsidiary)
podcast.body: Prompted by reports of strong sales in Boston, Malf Schlacht of Scepter Records decided to pick up The Kingsmen's "Louie Louie" for national distribution through their Wand subsidiary. "Malf Schlacht of its septer heard from the distributors how well the record was doing, and picked it up for national distribution on their one subsidiary."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Royalty Scandal and Lawsuits
podcast.body: Scepter Records, under Florence Greenberg's management, was involved in a major royalty dispute with The Shirelles. The group discovered that money promised for a trust fund was instead being kept by Greenberg, leading to lawsuits. Despite the legal battles, The Shirelles remained signed to Scepter, preventing them from recording for other labels and effectively destroying their career. "They entered into lawsuits against Septa, but remained sand to the label, and so couldn't record for anyone else. Their career was destroyed."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Tiny Label After Major Labels
podcast.body: Scepter was a tiny label that the Isley Brothers signed with after leaving Atlantic Records. This move represented a significant step down in label size, following their progression from a tiny indie to a large indie, and then to a major label. "and signing with a tiny label, Scepter."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
